note: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands have no bank of their own. The House of Representatives Standing Committee on the National Capital and External Territories, in chapter 5 of its report on communications in the Indian Ocean Territories (Island to Islands; the PDF was made on 18 March 1999), says there is no bank as such on Cocos but a Commonwealth Bank agent, from whose agency people cash cheques and draw money from their accounts, and that some people bank by phone with banks on the mainland. That agency is an agent of an Australian bank (the Commonwealth Bank of Australia), not a bank of the islands. AusPayNet's BSB directory (the full file, read 2026-10-30) lists no branch at the islands' postcode, 6799, or under their name. The report is old: no current statement of the islands' banking was reachable (the Department of Infrastructure's pages for the territory gave no answer, also over HTTP/1.1, and the Shire's site answered 403 on 2026-10-30), so this rests on the report and the directory's silence. A Wikipedia list naming the Commonwealth Bank there cites a tourism directory's business listing (2017), which agrees with an agency.

sources.title: Parliament of Australia, House of Representatives Standing Committee on the National Capital and External Territories, report on communications in the Indian Ocean Territories, chapter 5: Cocos (Keeling) Islands (PDF created 18 March 1999)
sources.said: There is no bank as such on Cocos Island; however there is a Commonwealth agent. ... People can cash their cheques or draw money from their accounts from the Commonwealth Bank agency. ... Some people conduct business banking by phone
